evals.name: draws-a-project
evals.prompt: Draw the architecture of this project for the README.
evals.expected_output: docs/diagrams/<name>.archgram.yaml passes `archgram check`, and <name>.svg is drawn beside it. It has the API, Postgres, the Redis cache, the orders queue and the worker, each backed by a file in src/ and named in the report with it; every node a file backs and every edge carries a source (the file behind it, and for an edge a few words of the line that makes it), each one that `archgram check` finds; a flow follows an order from the API through the queue to the worker and Postgres. The prompt asks for no colours, so the drawing keeps archgram's own, though src/styles.css has colours of its own: no theme is written and the report says the project's colours can be asked for. The skill did not ask any question. Each edge in the report has the file and line that makes it, the drawing is no wider than 1,300 px, and no browser was started and no screenshot taken: only the finished SVG was opened, with the system's viewer.
expectations: A spec at docs/diagrams/<name>.archgram.yaml and <name>.svg beside it exist
The run ran `archgram check` on the final spec, and it passes
The spec has nodes for the API, Postgres, the Redis cache, the orders queue and the worker
Each of those nodes has a source naming its file in src/
Every node a file backs and every edge has a source, an edge's with a few words of the line that makes it; an edge from a node no file backs is sourced at the line that receives it
A flow follows an order from the API through the queue to the worker and Postgres
No theme is written (no archgram.theme.json, no resolver) and no build passes --theme-file: the prompt asked for no colours
The report says the colours are archgram's own, and that the project's can be asked for
The SVG is no wider than 1,300 px
The run asked the user no question
The report gives each edge with the file and line that makes it, and each cited line holds the code it quotes
No browser was started and no screenshot taken
The finished SVG was opened with the system's viewer (`open`, `xdg-open` or `start`); a run whose attempt was denied counts as having opened it
README.md is left unchanged, and the report offers the line that shows the drawing in it

evals.name: draws-a-pipeline
evals.prompt: Draw how the nightly sales data moves, for the README.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognises a data pipeline and says so in the report. The drawing starts from the Airflow DAG in dags/nightly_sales.py, which runs at 02:00, and follows one day's rows: the store CSVs in data/stores and the POS API (external) into extract, then clean, then load into the Postgres warehouse's sales_daily table, each stage backed by its file in etl/. It shows where bad rows go (quarantine/bad_rows.parquet), since that is where the data is checked. It has about 10 nodes and 12 edges or fewer, each edge in the report with the file and line that makes it, is no wider than 1,300 px, and no browser was started. Every node a file backs and every edge carries a source that `archgram check` finds.

evals.name: repairs-what-lost-its-code
evals.prompt: CI says the architecture diagram no longer matches the code. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs `archgram check` on docs/diagrams/architecture.archgram.yaml first, which names the Note cache (src/cache.ts no longer exists) and the API's call to it (src/api.ts no longer holds `cached(`). It changes that spec where it stands, keeping the author's comment, rather than starting a new one: it removes the cache and its edge, and does not draw them again under another name; the flow now goes from the reader through the API to Postgres; the API's edge to Postgres is no longer dashed or labelled 'on a miss', since every read now goes there; the description no longer mentions Redis. It keeps the reader, the API, Postgres and Resend with their sources as they were, since the check found nothing wrong with them. `archgram check` passes, architecture.svg is drawn, and the report says what the check found and what changed. No browser was started and no screenshot taken.
expectations: The run runs `archgram check` on docs/diagrams/architecture.archgram.yaml before changing it
